read.en: ❼ Their three options were an art show, a bake sale, and a charity concert, but there were conflicting opinions.
read.ko: 그들의 세 가지 선택지는 미술 전시회, 빵 바자회, 그리고 자선 콘서트였지만, 상충되는 의견들이 있었다.

read.en: ❽ So they decided to put it to a vote.
read.ko: 그래서 그들은 그것을 투표에 부치기로 결정했다.

read.en: ❾ When they asked for advice from Ms. Akers, the council’s advisor, she encouraged them not to use the familiar voting method, but to try something different instead.
read.ko: 그들이 자치회의 고문 교사인 Akers 선생님에게 조언을 구했을 때, 그녀는 익숙한 투표 방법을 사용하지 말고, 대신 다른 것을 시도해 보라고 권장했다.

read.en: ❿ After doing some research, the council members decided to try three different voting systems: the first-past-the-post (FPTP) method, the alternative vote (AV) method, and the Condorcet method.
read.ko: 약간의 조사를 한 후, 자치회 구성원들은 단순 다수결(FPTP) 방식, 대안 투표(AV) 방식, 그리고 콩도르세 방식이라는 세 가지의 다른 투표 시스템을 시도해 보 기로 결정했다.

read.en: ⓫ The entire council was curious to find out if the different methods would yield different results.
read.ko: 모든 자치회 구성원들은 각각 다른 방법이 서로 다른 결과를 낼지 궁금해했다.

read.en: ⓬ On the day of the vote, each possible event was given a letter: “art show” was represented by the letter A, the letter B indicated “bake sale,” and C stood for “charity concert.”
read.ko: 투표 당일, 각각의 가능한 행사에 글자가 하나씩 부여되었다. ‘미술 전시회’는 글자 A로 표시되었고, 글자 B는 ‘빵 바자회’를 나타냈으며, C는 ‘자선 콘서트’를 의 미했다.

read.en: ⓭ Each of the 20 council members was given a voting slip and instructed to write down the options in order of preference.
read.ko: 20명의 자치회 구성원들 각각은 투표용지를 받았고, 선호하는 순서대로 선택지를 적으라는 지시를 받았다.

read.en: ⓮ For example, if the charity concert was their first choice, followed by the bake sale and the art show, they would write CBA.
read.ko: 예를 들어, 자선 콘서트가 첫 번째 선택이고 빵 바자회와 미술 전시회가 뒤따른다면, 그들은 CBA를 적을 것이다.

read.en: ⓯ After every member had voted, the voting slips were counted.
read.ko: 모든 구성원이 투표를 마친 후, 투표용지가 집계되었다.

read.en: ❶ The FPTP method is the simplest of the three methods.
read.ko: FPTP 방식은 세 가지 방식 중 가장 간단하다.

read.en: ❷ Voters are given several options, and whichever gets the most first-preference votes wins.
read.ko: 투표자들에게는 여러 가지 선택지가 주어지고, 어떤 것이든 가장 많은 1지망 표를 얻은 것이 이긴다.

read.en: ❸ Neither the second nor third preference matters at all, so they are ignored.
read.ko: 2지망도 3지망도 둘 다 전혀 중요하지 않으므로, 그것들은 무시된다.

read.en: ❹ This method is commonly used in political elections around the world.
read.ko: 이 방식은 전 세계 정치 선거에서 흔히 사용된다.

read.en: ❺ The student council quickly determined that the winner would be option C, the charity concert.
read.ko: 학생 자치회는 빠르게 자선 콘서트인 선택지 C가 승자가 될 것임을 알아냈다.

read.en: ❻ This was because it received 8 first-preference votes, while option A received 5 and option B received 7.
read.ko: 이는 선택지 A는 5표, 선택지 B는 7표를 받은 반면, 그것은 8표의 1지망 표를 받았기 때문이었다.

read.en: ❼ The FPTP method is uncomplicated and easy to understand, but it has a significant weakness.
read.ko: FPTP 방식은 복잡하지 않고 이해하기 쉽지만, 상당한 약점을 가지고 있다.

read.en: ❽ It is possible to win a vote without the support of the majority.
read.ko: 과반수의 지지 없이도 투표에서 승리하는 것이 가능하다.

read.en: ❾ That was the case here.
read.ko: 이것이 바로 그런 경우였다.

read.en: ❿ According to the results of the FPTP method, the council’s choice was to hold a charity concert.
read.ko: FPTP 방식의 결과에 따르면, 자치회의 선택은 자선 콘서트를 개최하는 것이었다.

read.en: ⓫ However, only 8 out of 20 council members chose the charity concert as their first preference, which equaled 40% of the total votes.
read.ko: 하지만 20명의 자치회 구성원 중 8명만이 1지망으로 자선 콘서트를 골랐는데, 이는 전체 표의 40%에 해당했다.

read.en: ❶ Next, the council members examined the votes using the AV method, and they soon realized that there would be a different result.
read.ko: 다음으로, 자치회 구성원들은 AV 방식을 사용하여 표를 검토했고, 그들은 곧 다른 결과가 나올 것이라는 것을 깨달았다.

read.en: ❷ The AV method can potentially include more than one round of counting.
read.ko: AV 방식은 잠재적으로 한 차례 이상의 집계를 포함할 수 있다.

read.en: ❸ For an option to win in the first round, it needs to get more than 50% of the first-preference votes.
read.ko: 어떤 선택지가 1차 집계에서 승리하기 위해서는, 1지망 표의 50% 이상을 얻어야 한다.

read.en: ❹ As the charity concert only received 40% of the total votes, a second round of counting was required.
read.ko: 자선 콘서트는 전체 표의 40%만을 받았기 때문에, 2차 집계가 필요했다.

read.en: ❺ Option A, the art show, received the fewest first-preference votes, with only 5 council members voting for it.
read.ko: 미술 전시회인 선택지 A는 오직 5명의 자치회 구성원들만 그것에 투표하며 가장 적은 1지망 표를 받았다.

read.en: ❻ Therefore, option A was eliminated, and the 5 council members’ votes were redistributed based on their second preferences.
read.ko: 따라서 선택지 A는 제거되었고, 5명의 자치회 구성원들의 표가 그들의 두 번째 선호도에 따라 재분배되었다.

read.en: ❼ As a result, 4 votes for option B (ABC) and 1 for option C (ACB) were added to the total.
read.ko: 그 결과, 선택지 B에 4표(ABC), 선택지 C에 1표(ACB)가 합계에 추가되었다.

read.en: ❽ This meant that option B had 11 total votes, while option C had only 9.
read.ko: 이것은 선택지 C는 9표밖에 얻지 못한 반면 선택지 B가 총 11표를 얻었다는 것을 의미했다.

read.en: ❾ As a result, the bake sale would be the winner.
read.ko: 결과적으로, 빵 바자회가 승자가 될 것이었다.

read.en: ❿ Unfortunately, the AV method is not perfect either.
read.ko: 안타깝게도, AV 방식도 완벽하지는 않다.

read.en: ⓫ It sometimes allows second-preference votes to have a greater influence than first-preference votes.
read.ko: 그것은 때때로 2지망 표가 1지망 표보다 더 큰 영향력을 갖게 하기도 한다.

read.en: ⓬ In this case, the bake sale won, but this was mainly due to the second-preference votes it received.
read.ko: 이 경우에는 빵 바자회가 승리했지만, 이는 주로 그것이 얻은 2지망 표 때문이었다.

read.en: ❶ Finally, the student council counted the votes using the Condorcet method.
read.ko: 마지막으로, 학생 자치회는 콩도르세 방식을 사용하여 표를 집계했다.

read.en: ❷ This method involves comparing the voters’ preferences between each possible pair of options.
read.ko: 이 방식은 가능한 선택지 쌍에 대한 투표자들의 선호도를 비교하는 것을 수반한다.

read.en: ❸ In this case, there were three pairs to consider: A vs. B, B vs. C, and A vs. C.
read.ko: 이 경우에는, 고려해야 할 세 쌍이 있었는데, 그것은 바로 A와 B, B와 C, A와 C였다.

read.en: ❹ Through this method, the student council discovered that its members preferred option A to option B by a count of 11 to 9.
read.ko: 이 방식을 통해, 학생 자치회는 구성원들이 11대 9로 선택지 B보다 선택지 A를 선호한다는 사실을 발견했다.

read.en: ❺ In other words, 11 people preferred A to B, voting either ABC, ACB, or CAB.
read.ko: 즉, 11명이 ABC, ACB, CAB 중 하나에 투표하며 B보다 A를 선호했다.

read.en: ❻ Meanwhile, 9 people preferred B to A by voting BAC, BCA, or CBA.
read.ko: 한편, 9명은 BAC, BCA 또는 CBA에 투표함으로써 A보다 B를 선호했다.

read.en: ❼ Interestingly, the voters preferred option B to option C by the same count of 11 to 9.
read.ko: 흥미롭게도, 투표자들은 동일하게 11대 9로 선택지 C보다 선택지 B를 선호했다.

read.en: ❽ They also preferred option A to option C by 11 to 9.
read.ko: 그들은 또한 11대 9로 선택지 C보다 선택지 A를 선호했다.

read.en: ❾ As option A, the art show, was preferred to both of the other options, it would be considered the winner.
read.ko: 미술 전시회인 선택지 A가 나머지 두 선택지보다 더 선호되었으므로, 이 선택지가 승자로 간주될 것이었다.

read.en: ❿ The Condorcet method’s weakness is that, along with being complex, it sometimes fails to select a winner.
read.ko: 콩도르세 방식의 약점은 복잡하다는 것과 더불어 때때로 승자를 가려내지 못한다는 점이다.

read.en: ⓫ This is especially true in elections that contain numerous options.
read.ko: 이는 많은 선택지를 포함하는 선거에서 특히 그렇다.

read.en: ⓬ It is possible that no option will be clearly preferred over the others.
read.ko: 어떤 선택지도 다른 선택지들보다 명확하게 선호되지 않을 수 있다.

read.en: ❶ Instead of all methods pointing toward a single option and making the council’s choice easier, the winner differed with each method.
read.ko: 모든 방식이 하나의 선택지를 가리키고 자치회의 선택을 더 쉽게 만드는 대신, 각 방식마다 승자는 달랐다.

read.en: ❷ After a long, intense discussion with Ms. Akers, the student council members decided to choose the Condorcet method, as they liked the idea of directly comparing each option with the others.
read.ko: Akers 선생님과의 오랜 열정적인 논의 끝에, 학생 자치회 구성원들은 콩도르세 방식을 선택하기로 결정했는데, 각 선택지를 다른 선택지들과 직접적으로 비교 한다는 점이 마음에 들었기 때문이다.

read.en: ❸ Everyone agreed that they learned a lot about different voting systems through this experience.
read.ko: 모두가 이번 경험을 통해 각기 다른 투표 시스템에 대해 많은 것을 배웠다는 것에 동의했다.

read.en: ❹ It is obvious that choosing an ideal voting method is a complex and challenging task.
read.ko: 이상적인 투표 방법을 선택하는 것은 복잡하고 도전적인 일이라는 것은 분명하다.

read.en: ❺ No voting system is flawless or clearly superior to another.
read.ko: 어떤 투표 시스템도 완벽하거나 다른 시스템보다 명백히 우수하지는 않다.

read.en: ❻ Whichever we choose will have pros and cons.
read.ko: 우리가 선택하는 어느 것이든 장단점이 있을 것이다.

read.en: ❼ Some people believe that it is best to keep the process simple by not ranking our choices at all.
read.ko: 어떤 사람들은 우리들의 선택들에 아예 순위를 매기지 않음으로써 과정을 단순하게 유지하는 것이 최선이라고 생각한다.

read.en: ❽ Others continue to develop and test new ways of voting, arguing that more complex methods deliver more accurate results.
read.ko: 다른 사람들은 더 복잡한 방식이 더 정확한 결과를 가져온다고 주장하며 계속해서 새로운 투표 방법을 개발하고 시험한다.

read.en: ❾ All of these efforts are designed not to make decision-making difficult and inefficient, but to help us make better decisions as a society.
read.ko: 이러한 모든 노력은 의사 결정을 어렵고 비효율적으로 만들기 위한 것이 아니라, 우리가 사회로서 더 나은 의사 결정을 내릴 수 있게 돕기 위해 고안된 것이다.

read.en: ❿ Ultimately, understanding all of the possible voting methods and weighing their pros and cons allows us to better understand the process of decision-making.
read.ko: 결국, 모든 가능한 투표 방법을 이해하고 장단점을 따져 보는 것은 우리가 의사 결정 과정을 더 잘 이해할 수 있게 한다.

read.en: ⓫ When we understand decision-making better, we are more likely to become better decision-makers ourselves.
read.ko: 우리가 의사 결정을 더 잘 이해할 때, 우리 스스로 더 나은 의사 결정자가 될 가능성이 더 높다.

para.en: ❶ We make many personal choices in our lives, from who to have lunch with to what career to pursue. ❷ However, there are many situations where we must make decisions as a group. ❸ Group decision-making is not as simple as our personal choices, as it involves numerous voices with differing opinions. ❹ Voting is often used to make group decisions fairer and more efficient, and various voting methods have been developed over time. ❺ The following story illustrates how these different voting methods work. ❻ The members of the Greenville High School student council needed to decide how to raise money for children in need. ❼ Their three options were an art show, a bake sale, and a charity concert, but there were conflicting opinions. ❽ So they decided to put it to a vote. ❾ When they asked for advice from Ms. Akers, the council’s advisor, she encouraged them not to use the familiar voting method, but to try something different instead. ❿ After doing some research, the council members decided to try three different voting systems: the first-past-the-post (FPTP) method, the alternative vote (AV) method, and the Condorcet method. ⓫ The entire council was curious to find out if the different methods would yield different results. ⓬ On the day of the vote, each possible event was given a letter: “art show” was represented by the letter A, the letter B indicated “bake sale,” and C stood for “charity concert.” ⓭ Each of the 20 council members was given a voting slip and instructed to write down the options in order of preference. ⓮ For example, if the charity concert was their first choice, followed by the bake sale and the art show, they would write CBA. ⓯ After every member had voted, the voting slips were counted.

❶ The FPTP method is the simplest of the three methods. ❷ Voters are given several options, and whichever gets the most first-preference votes wins. ❸ Neither the second nor third preference matters at all, so they are ignored. ❹ This method is commonly used in political elections around the world. ❺ The student council quickly determined that the winner would be option C, the charity concert. ❻ This was because it received 8 first-preference votes, while option A received 5 and option B received 7. ❼ The FPTP method is uncomplicated and easy to understand, but it has a significant weakness. ❽ It is possible to win a vote without the support of the majority. ❾ That was the case here. ❿ According to the results of the FPTP method, the council’s choice was to hold a charity concert. ⓫ However, only 8 out of 20 council members chose the charity concert as their first preference, which equaled 40% of the total votes.

❶ Next, the council members examined the votes using the AV method, and they soon realized that there would be a different result. ❷ The AV method can potentially include more than one round of counting. ❸ For an option to win in the first round, it needs to get more than 50% of the first-preference votes. ❹ As the charity concert only received 40% of the total votes, a second round of counting was required. ❺ Option A, the art show, received the fewest first-preference votes, with only 5 council members voting for it. ❻ Therefore, option A was eliminated, and the 5 council members’ votes were redistributed based on their second preferences. ❼ As a result, 4 votes for option B (ABC) and 1 for option C (ACB) were added to the total. ❽ This meant that option B had 11 total votes, while option C had only 9. ❾ As a result, the bake sale would be the winner. ❿ Unfortunately, the AV method is not perfect either. ⓫ It sometimes allows second-preference votes to have a greater influence than first-preference votes. ⓬ In this case, the bake sale won, but this was mainly due to the second-preference votes it received.

❶ Finally, the student council counted the votes using the Condorcet method. ❷ This method involves comparing the voters’ preferences between each possible pair of options. ❸ In this case, there were three pairs to consider: A vs. B, B vs. C, and A vs. C. ❹ Through this method, the student council discovered that its members preferred option A to option B by a count of 11 to 9. ❺ In other words, 11 people preferred A to B, voting either ABC, ACB, or CAB. ❻ Meanwhile, 9 people preferred B to A by voting BAC, BCA, or CBA. ❼ Interestingly, the voters preferred option B to option C by the same count of 11 to 9. ❽ They also preferred option A to option C by 11 to 9. ❾ As option A, the art show, was preferred to both of the other options, it would be considered the winner. ❿ The Condorcet method’s weakness is that, along with being complex, it sometimes fails to select a winner. ⓫ This is especially true in elections that contain numerous options. ⓬ It is possible that no option will be clearly preferred over the others.

❶ Instead of all methods pointing toward a single option and making the council’s choice easier, the winner differed with each method. ❷ After a long, intense discussion with Ms. Akers, the student council members decided to choose the Condorcet method, as they liked the idea of directly comparing each option with the others. ❸ Everyone agreed that they learned a lot about different voting systems through this experience. ❹ It is obvious that choosing an ideal voting method is a complex and challenging task. ❺ No voting system is flawless or clearly superior to another. ❻ Whichever we choose will have pros and cons. ❼ Some people believe that it is best to keep the process simple by not ranking our choices at all. ❽ Others continue to develop and test new ways of voting, arguing that more complex methods deliver more accurate results. ❾ All of these efforts are designed not to make decision-making difficult and inefficient, but to help us make better decisions as a society. ❿ Ultimately, understanding all of the possible voting methods and weighing their pros and cons allows us to better understand the process of decision-making. ⓫ When we understand decision-making better, we are more likely to become better decision-makers ourselves.

howto.cloze: 빈칸을 하나씩 보여 줘요. 우리말 뜻·유의어·첫 글자 힌트를 보고 원문 표현 그대로 쓰고 Enter(또는 다음 빈칸)를 누르세요. 빈칸을 모두 채워야 다음 지문으로 넘어가요.
howto.tf: 글과 일치하면 T, 아니면 F를 누르세요. 문장을 하나씩 보여 주고, 누르면 다음 문장으로 넘어가요. 지문은 아래 상자 안에서 스크롤하며 읽어요. 결과 화면에서 F 문장의 고칠 부분과 근거를 확인하세요.
